messages:
lina: FYI escalated from enterprise customer — after running their CI which installs our Python SDK they get a pip hash verification failure, then an ImportError when they try to import redwood.client

lina: Quick summary they use poetry in CI to build a wheel, then a separate step pip-installs that wheel into a simple venv image. Errors below. Any ideas before I ask for full repro?

morgan: Do we have a known issue with our sdist/wheel hashes changing between builds? Could be build metadata or non-deterministic timestamp in packaging.

lina: Paste from CI job (redacted):
```
Collecting redwood-inference==1.4.2
  Using cached https://packages.example.com/redwood-inference-1.4.2-py3-none-any.whl (12 kB)
  WARNING: The hashes for the following files do not match the expected hashes:
    redwood-inference-1.4.2-py3-none-any.whl
  Aborting installation.
  If you want to skip this verification, you can use --no-deps or --no-binary, etc.
```

lina: Followed by their local repro using pip install of wheel (same checksum mismatch) and then a fallback build which produced a wheel with different hash and ImportError: cannot import name 'RedwoodClient' from 'redwood'

tj: Two quick paths: (1) this is a packaging/build pipeline problem — wheel contents differ between the built artifact and what's being fetched. (2) They might be mixing editable installs or path dependencies so poetry lock pinned a different build. Ask them: are they using poetry export --with-hashes + pip --require-hashes?

lina: They said: yes, CI does `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes -o reqs.txt` then pip install -r reqs.txt. They also have an earlier step that builds wheel via `poetry build` and uploads to their private repo. Not using --require-hashes in pip, but the host registry enforces content verification at download time (digest check).

morgan: Could be timestamps in our wheel metadata (PEP 517 build) if build environment varies. Also check if their packaging step rebuilds from source rather than consuming the artifact uploaded to registry — double-build mismatch.

lina: Repro steps they used (from customer):
```
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
pip install https://packages.example.com/redwood-inference-1.4.2-py3-none-any.whl
# -> HASH mismatch
# they downloaded wheel and ran `unzip -l redwood-inference-1.4.2-py3-none-any.whl` and saw different file list than their build artifact
```

tj: Actionable guidance: 1) Ask them to compute sha256 of the wheel file on the CI machine right after upload and compare to the one pip fetches. 2) If they rebuild locally, ensure build environment and version of build tools (setuptools/poetry/build backend) are pinned. 3) Try `pip download --no-deps` and `pip install --no-deps` to rule out registry-side verification interference.

morgan: Also ask if they have a proxy/cache (artifactory) that might be serving a stale or corrupted file. If so, purge cache.

lina: I pinged them for the wheel sha256 and they replied with two different values from two runners. They also admitted they have a build matrix that produces wheels on linux:ubuntu-latest and linux:debian-latest and upload both to the same path (bad).

tj: Ok that's the root cause then — non-deterministic artifact path collision. Proposed message for customer: explain that the checksum mismatch is because different runners produced different wheels and only one version ends up in the registry at a time; suggest unique artifact names (include short git sha) or use a canonical build pipeline that publishes once. Also include short remediation steps: clear registry cache, reupload canonical wheel, and verify import locally.

lina: Drafted response and included commands they can run to verify:
```
# compute local sha256
python -c "import hashlib,sys;print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read()).hexdigest())" dist/redwood_inference-1.4.2-py3-none-any.whl
# download via pip and compute
pip download --no-deps https://packages.example.com/redwood-inference-1.4.2-py3-none-any.whl -d /tmp && python -c "import hashlib,sys;print(hashlib.sha256(open('/tmp/redwood-inference-1.4.2-py3-none-any.whl','rb').read()).hexdigest())"
```

morgan: 👍 Also add a note to our docs: recommend artifact naming that includes build id/commit to avoid registry collisions. Maybe we should add a short KB entry for support about "hash mismatch when installing SDK wheel" with these triage steps.

devex-bot: Created support KB draft ticket #SUP-8421 (owner: morgan) :link:

lina: Thanks — I'll send the remediation and keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
